audits.title: Revisiting Dental Care and Mental Health: A Quality Improvement Project of Dental Care for Patients With Severe Mental Illness Living in a Community Rehabilitation Centre
audits.standard: NICE oral health quality standards: mouth care needs assessed on admission, recorded in care plan, and support for twice-daily tooth cleaning and denture care
audits.setting: Lime Tree Gardens, care home/community rehabilitation centre for adults with severe mental illness

cycle1.result: More than 90% of patients had unmet oral health needs.

audits.citation: Wang Y, Singh S, Duah L, Salih S, Allin M. Revisiting Dental Care and Mental Health: A Quality Improvement Project of Dental Care for Patients With Severe Mental Illness Living in a Community Rehabilitation Centre. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S177-S177. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.450.

audits.title: Monitoring Oral Hygiene in Inpatient Psychiatric Units: A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: Trust inpatient policy: comprehensive physical health assessment including oral health examination on admission, and dental hygiene in ongoing nursing care reviews
audits.setting: Inpatient mental health units (acute, older adult, low-secure forensic, rehabilitation), Derbyshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 'Eating, Drinking and Oral Health' questionnaire partially completed for 61.4% (70/114), fully completed for none. Formal oral health examination recorded for 10.5% (12/114), 0% in forensic unit. No patients had a completed oral health risk assessment.

audits.other_findings: Of 30 patients with acute dental issues during admission, 18 accessed professional dental care, with variation between ward types.
audits.citation: Mohdesham Z, Tandon K, Rozza A, Sidhu J, Us-Saba N. Monitoring Oral Hygiene in Inpatient Psychiatric Units: A Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S320-S321. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11662.

audits.title: An audit of oral care practice and staff knowledge in hospital palliative care.
audits.standard: Oral care practice (assessment, implementation, prescribing, evaluation) and staff knowledge
audits.setting: Hospital palliative care, Newark Hospital (central England)

cycle1.result: Baseline audit of oral care practice and nursing knowledge; numbers not reported.

audits.intervention: Oral care guidelines and a programme of ward-based teaching were introduced.

cycle2.result: Improvement in all aspects of oral care and staff knowledge (numbers not reported).

audits.other_findings: Additional benefits included improved professional relationships and promotion of further palliative care audits.
audits.citation: Lee L, White V, Ball J, Gill K, Smart L, McEwan K, et al.. An audit of oral care practice and staff knowledge in hospital palliative care. Int J Palliat Nurs. 2001;7(8):395-400. doi:10.12968/ijpn.2001.7.8.9011. PMID: 11951784.

audits.title: Mouth care in cancer nursing: using an audit to change practice.
audits.standard: Mouth care practice and staff knowledge
audits.setting: Oncology unit, University Hospitals of Leicester, large teaching hospital

cycle1.result: Oral problems common but under-reported, underdiagnosed, inadequately treated and inadequately documented; nursing knowledge deficits.

audits.intervention: Oral care guidelines, patient information leaflets, posters and staff education programme.

cycle2.result: Significant improvements in diagnosis and treatment of oral problems and increased patient reporting (numbers not reported).

audits.citation: Honnor A, Law A. Mouth care in cancer nursing: using an audit to change practice. Br J Nurs. 2002;11(16):1087-1096. doi:10.12968/bjon.2002.11.16.10550. PMID: 12362137.

audits.title: Improving the oral health of older adults with dementia/cognitive impairment living in a residential aged care facility.
audits.standard: JBI best practice criteria for oral hygiene care
audits.setting: Residential aged care facility, northern Adelaide
audits.intervention: Strategic change-management plan by a project team targeting specific criteria.

cycle2.result: Denture marking compliance increased significantly; documentation of denture cleaning and night-time removal increased slightly (not significant).

audits.citation: Georg D. Improving the oral health of older adults with dementia/cognitive impairment living in a residential aged care facility. Int J Evid Based Healthc. 2006;4(1):54-61. doi:10.1111/j.1479-6988.2006.00032.x. PMID: 21631755.
